STEP 1 - Scene: This is a pile of raw (unroasted, unsalted-looking) almonds on a white square plate, photographed from above at a near top-down angle. It is a snack portion, not a full meal.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate measures roughly 24 cm across its width (the almonds are about 2.5 cm long each, which fits this scale). Plate area ≈ 24 × 24 × ~0.8 (rounded corners) ≈ 460 cm². Using a circular approximation of a 24 cm diameter gives 3.14 × 12² ≈ 452 cm²; I use ~450 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: Whole almonds (shelled, brown skins, raw/natural).

STEP 4 - Area: The almond pile covers roughly 45% of the plate area (the pile sits in the upper-left-centre region, with gaps at the edges). Almonds: 45% ≈ 200 cm².

STEP 5 - Volume: The pile is about 2 almonds high on average, with a typical height of ~1.5 cm for a loose heap. Gross volume ≈ 200 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 300 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Almonds are dense, but a loose heap of whole nuts has a bulk density of about 0.5–0.6 g/ml. Using 0.55: 300 ml × 0.55 ≈ 165 g.

Sanity check: Count check: roughly 90–100 almonds are visible, and an almond weighs about 1.2 g, so ~110–120 g. This is consistent with the volume estimate, so I take about 130 g as a middle value.

STEP 7 - Energy: Raw almonds ≈ 579 kcal/100 g. 130 g × 5.79 ≈ 753 kcal.

Result: about 130 g of almonds, about 750 kcal.
